title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-11
content:
Quick notes / dump for the day - mostly TODOs and triage.

SUMMARY
- Focus: perf regressions after kernel bump (nvfuser -> xla-ish path) and recent KV-cache miss spikes.
- Goal: get stable 95th percentile latency back under 120ms for small-chat workloads (seq_len ~128) on p4d.

OPEN BUGS / TRIAGE
- BUG-5531: intermittent 95p latency spike on small-chat. Repro hits on canary in eu-west-1 between 06:00-09:00 UTC.
  - Symptoms: sudden 2-3x increase in generation tail for ~5-10m windows. No allocation OOMs.
  - Hypothesis: kernel selection fallback causing non-optimized path and disabling continuous batching.
  - Logs to check: /var/log/redwood/serving/runtime-canary-*/kernel-selector.log
  - Quick repro: run loadgen with --seq=128 --qps=30 for 20m against canary. If spike appears, collect perf counters.
  - Next: add extra debug around kernel decision (trace kselect) and add histogram of selected kernel per request.

- BUG-5599: KV-cache miss rate jumped from ~2% to 7% after deploy abc123 (quantized cache refactor).
  - Symptoms: more repeated prefix recomputation and higher token compute.
  - Hypothesis: cache key hashing changed for quantized shards -> mismatch when routing between hosts.
  - Action: revert hashing tweak on canary, run sheep test (multi-worker random routing) for 6h.
  - Temp mitigation: force sticky routing for known heavy prefixes (route_policy:sticky_prefixes) until fix.

PERF EXPERIMENTS / TODOs
- Experiment A: kernel warmup microbench (today)
  - Run: tools/bench/kernel-warmup.sh --model llama-13b --seq 128 --batch 1..8 --reps 200
  - Measure: kernel compile times, first-token latency, subsequent token throughput.
  - Compare nvfuser vs xla-ish path vs new-fused-kernels.
  - Note: watch for disk IO spikes during JIT compile (limit concurrent compiles).

- Experiment B: batching policy adjust
  - Try: reduce max-latency-ms from 20 -> 10 for interactive route; increase max-batch-size from 8 -> 12 for background embed route.
  - Goal: see impact on 50/95/99 percentiles and token-cost. Run for 4h window on staging.

- Experiment C: prefix cache TTL tuning
  - Current TTL: 5m for ephemeral prefixes; consider 15m for stable traffic (product chat).
  - Monitoring: cache hit rate, memory usage, eviction churn.

KERNEL NOTES (brain dump)
- Observed: kernel-selector sometimes picks scalar fallback on mixed-quant models when batch size changes mid-request (weird). Add unit tests that simulate batch-size change across microbatches.
- Potential fix: add explicit 'force_vectorized' flag for certain op sequences (attention softmax + rotary) when seq_len < 256.
- Follow-up: re-evaluate register pressure for fused-attn on A100 vs H100. Some microbenchmarks show H100 benefits more from split-kernel approach.

RUNBOOK UPDATES (short)
- Add a dashboard tile: kernel-selection-by-host (heatmap) + kernel-selection-by-model-version.
- Alert: if KV-cache miss_rate > 5% for >10m -> page oncall and route to eng-serving-runtime.

ACTION ITEMS (priority ordered)
1) Add kernel selection tracing to canary (Alex) - today
   - patch: add trace id + kernel name to request span
   - PR: start from pr/1789 (kernel refactor) -> add toggles
2) Revert cache-hash tweak on canary and run sheep test (Diego) - today
3) Run kernel warmup microbench and upload results to confluence (Priya) - tomorrow AM
4) Adjust batching policy on staging and compare histograms (Alex) - tomorrow PM
5) Write unit tests for batch-size-change edge cases (owner: Alex) - end of week

NOTES / CLI SNIPPETS
- quick repro loadgen: ./tools/loadgen --target canary.internal.redwood --model llama-13b --seq 128 --qps 30 --duration 1200 --log-level debug
- collect kernel traces: ssh canary && sudo journalctl -u serving -f | grep kernel-selector > /tmp/kselect.log
- sheep test: infra/scripts/sheep_test.sh --hosts 10 --duration 21600 --route random

QUESTIONS / DISCUSS LATER
- Should kernel selection be sticky per-connection to avoid oscillation mid-conversation? Tradeoff: might pick suboptimal kernel for some message shapes.
- Long-term: unified kernel registry with capability tags vs current heuristic selector. Do we want capability tags (vector-length, supports-quant) in model metadata?

RANDOM TODO (low priority)
- port perf-ci job to run nightly on H100 pool (currently only runs A100).
- check if quantized-cache uses same eviction policy across dedicated vs hosted (consistency needed).

END OF SCRATCHPAD

(Will clean up into a proper bug tickets and a confluence writeup after initial triage)
